classification: construction-feasibility-probe; not a runtime qualification or formal WSLc allocation
question: Can a caller return by one absolute cancellation deadline while worker process startup is delayed inside an already-ready supervisor, and can a Fake X state oracle independently reject a stale-generation or late KeyRelease?
runtime: Windows host; Python multiprocessing spawn; loopback Fake X state server; no X server, Xlib, physical input, WSL, WSLc, Docker, or external model

synchronous-delayed-start.expected: caller misses deadline; late worker refuses effect; input remains down and result is unknown

prestarted-supervisor-delayed-start.expected: caller returns unknown within deadline plus slack; late worker refuses effect; input remains down

prestarted-supervisor-fast-control.expected: Fake X accepts exactly one KeyRelease before deadline and independent state readback reports key up

prestarted-supervisor-stale-generation.expected: Fake X rejects old generation; key remains down; caller reports unknown

frozen_inputs.generation: unique per trial; stale arm sends the preceding generation
frozen_inputs.deadline_clock: time.monotonic_ns shared by parent and spawned children
frozen_inputs.launch_delay_injection: sleep in the Process.start wrapper immediately before the real start call

decision.pass: all six delayed-start trials meet their arm-specific response/effect expectations; all three fast controls release and read back up; all three stale controls are rejected; every raw row is retained
decision.fail: any delayed prestarted call exceeds 450 ms, any KeyRelease is accepted after deadline or under stale generation, any fast control lacks independent key-up readback, or any trial receipt is missing
decision.scope_limit: A PASS demonstrates only the constructed control-flow property. It does not qualify production supervisor code, actual X11/XTEST, blocked server I/O, caller integration, input release guarantees, MAP01, or reliability.
